thread:
alex.lewis: got woken up by a PagerDuty page for service 'realtime-inference' — odd, I'm not on that rota anymore :confused:
pd_bot: PagerDuty notification: Incident INC-202503 - Triggered on service realtime-inference, urgency: high, triggered by check 'latency_alert'
sre_bot: incident-bot: Page fired and escalation started -> routed to schedule 'infra-rotation' (bound to infra@company).
maria_g: i also got the page. i'm on ml-platform schedule, why did infra get it?
ops_oncall: same here — i'm on the ml-platform rota but the page went to infra and also to some contractors list.
kirill: checking PD bindings now. can someone run `pd schedule get realtime-inference`?
jenna: running it: ```
$ pd schedule get realtime-inference
name: realtime-inference
bindings:
  - schedule: infra-rotation
  - schedule: ml-platform
last_updated: 2025-03-12T02:12:08Z
propagation_state: queued
```
alex.lewis: aha "propagation_state: queued" — that looks like the new rota edits didn't finish propagating; we just changed bindings an hour ago to move primary to ml-platform.
maria_g: that matches — I removed infra from primary per last week's change, but PD web UI showed unbound until ~1h ago.
pd_bot: PagerDuty: note — schedule-update webhook delivery failed for integration 'rota-syncer' (HTTP 504).
ops_oncall: rota-syncer 504 — we saw similar earlier where calendar imports hit a timeout and PD left stale binding. is rota-syncer our syncer to PD?
kirill: yes, rota-syncer pushes oncall schedules from HR calendar -> PagerDuty. Looks like a transient gateway timeout; it retried and partially applied, leaving both schedules bound. That caused PD to fanout pages to both infra and ml-platform depending on which worker answered first.
sre_bot: impact check: did customers experience degraded responses? metric check: p50 latency bumped to 1.2s for 2 mins at 02:11 UTC, error rate unchanged. no downstream 5xx spike.
jenna: customer-facing? alert from monitoring was latency-only, no user-facing errors per logs. I'd mark impact as "potentially degraded" until we confirm.
alex.lewis: immediate mitigation: 1) silence duplicate escalation rules for realtime-inference (temp). 2) re-run rota-syncer push with forced full-sync. 3) if pages continue, escalate to SRE manager to trigger PD manual rebind.
maria_g: i'll silence via PD UI for 10m on escalation policy to stop duplicate pages. doing now -> :white_check_mark:
ops_oncall: i'm forcing a full sync: `rota-syncer --force-sync --target realtime-inference` -> returns `200 OK, applied 1 changes`
pd_bot: PagerDuty: Full sync acknowledged, current bindings: primary: ml-platform, secondary: infra (standby).
kirill: confirming — PD now shows ml-platform as primary; propagation state: applied.
jenna: monitoring shows page rate dropped to normal, latency trending back down.
sre_bot: long-term action item: investigate rota-syncer 504s during peak calendar write windows. add retry/backoff and detection for partial-apply.
alex.lewis: tagging for postmortem: we need timeline, root cause (gateway timeout -> partial apply), why PD didn't prefer primary only, and a runbook to force single-binding and to mute duplicates quickly.
maria_g: do we need to notify customers? ops: impact was very brief and only latency. i'd prefer a short note if any customers contacted us; none in the support queue so far.
ops_oncall: support queue empty, no customer-reported incidents. marking customer impact: none observed.
kirill: filed incident ticket: INC-202503-ONCALLSYNC, assigned to rota-team, priority P2.
jenna: adding follow-up tasks: - add health-check & alert for rota-syncer webhook failures - add idempotent apply logic to avoid partial-binding - add runbook step to check `propagation_state` before trusting UI changes
alex.lewis: thanks all — closing this slack thread once PD autocloses INC-202503. leaving notes in incident board. :thumbsup:
